prompt: Match each situation to the commitment that fits it.
hint: Specific and steady, or a mix that moves?

pairs.left: Two D4s v5 VMs that run all year in brazilsouth
Compute spend that moves between VMs and Container Apps
Instances that run only in business-hour peaks

prompt: What happens to a reserved hour when no matching VM runs in it?

choices.text: It carries over to the next hour
choices.why: Unused hours do not carry over.

choices.text: It is refunded at the end of the month
choices.why: There is no refund for unused hours.

choices.text: It is lost
choices.why: Right. That is the whole risk of committing.

choices.text: It is charged at pay-as-you-go rates
choices.why: It is paid at the reserved rate, with nothing to show for it.

prompt: Why is the average, 2.87 instances, the wrong size for the workers' reservation?
hint: How many hours ran exactly two?

choices.text: Reservations must be whole numbers above the average
choices.why: No such rule; the floor is what matters.

choices.text: A third reserved instance idles in 480 hours
choices.why: Right. Commit to the floor, not the mean.

choices.text: The average includes weekends, which are free
choices.why: Weekends are billed like any other hours.

choices.text: The median is always lower than the average
choices.why: Not always; and the floor is the measure here.

prompt: In the month of WorkerHours, how many hours ran exactly two instances?
Why does a real decision use three months or more rather than this lesson's one?

choices.text: Reservations need three months of history to be bought
choices.why: No such requirement exists.

choices.text: Because a month has too few hours to compute a percentile
choices.why: 720 hours is plenty for a percentile.

choices.text: A seasonal low might not be in one month
choices.why: Right. The floor has to hold for the whole term.

choices.text: To average out the business-hour peaks
choices.why: Peaks are paid as you go anyway; the floor is the question.

prompt: In commit.kql's answer, what does the month cost with 2 instances reserved, in USD?
Committing to 3 instances discounts more of the month's usage than committing to 2. Why does it cost more?

choices.text: The reserved rate rises with the size
choices.why: The rate is the same per instance-hour.

choices.text: Pay-as-you-go hours become more expensive
choices.why: The pay-as-you-go rate is fixed.

choices.text: The query double-counts the third instance
choices.why: It counts each committed instance once per hour.

choices.text: The third instance is paid in hours it idles
choices.why: Right. 22% of the committed hours had nothing to cover.

prompt: What is the shop's order for covering its compute?

choices.text: Reserve the floor, savings plan the rest, peaks as you go
choices.why: Right. Each tool covers the usage it fits.

choices.text: Savings plan for everything, including peaks
choices.why: Peaks would leave committed dollars unused off-peak.

choices.text: Reserve the maximum, so that nothing is ever paid as you go
choices.why: That wastes most of the reservation most of the time.

choices.text: No commitments, since prices are illustrative
choices.why: Illustrative prices are for the lesson; the shape holds with real ones.

prompt: What does Azure Hybrid Benefit remove from a Windows VM's hourly rate?

choices.text: The compute it runs on
choices.why: Compute is still paid, or discounted by a reservation.

choices.text: The Windows licence
choices.why: Right. You use the licence you already hold.

choices.text: The managed disk
choices.why: Disks are billed separately and unaffected.

choices.text: Network egress charges
choices.why: Egress has nothing to do with licences.

prompt: A team switches Hybrid Benefit on for forty Windows VMs to save money, without counting licences. What is the risk?

choices.text: Azure refuses the setting until it sees proof
choices.why: Azure accepts it; the organisation asserts eligibility.

choices.text: The VMs stop running
choices.why: They run normally.

choices.text: An audit finds licences that were never there
choices.why: Right. You must hold and count them.

choices.text: The reservation on those VMs is cancelled
choices.why: The two combine; neither cancels the other.

prompt: Which statements about this lesson are true? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: The rates used are illustrative
choices.why: Yes. The price list was out of reach.

choices.text: Committing to the floor was the cheapest of the four sizes
choices.why: Yes. 387.40 USD.

choices.text: A reservation was bought for the shop
choices.why: No. Reservations are billing objects in a real account.

choices.text: Hybrid Benefit applies to the shop's Linux App Service
choices.why: No. There is no licence in that rate to remove.
